role: Scheme B alternate wall/ceiling pair — lighter warm ecru walls with Virgin White ceiling

scheme_a_unchanged.note: Scheme A remains the default locked concept: NN9074 Puddle of Grey walls + WW0005 White Linen ceiling.

walls.name: Ecru Tint
walls.use_rule: Scheme B walls throughout (lighter alternative to NN9074). Prefer washable system; shows dust/smoke faster than mid-tone greige.

ceiling.name: Virgin White
ceiling.use_rule: Scheme B ceilings only. Cleaner/warmer-leaning white than WW0005 White Linen; pairs with NN9088 Ecru Tint.

decision.rationale: Official Birla Opus catalogue lists Virgin White as WW 0020. Local project shade-card extract and birlaopus.com both give RGB 237,233,226 (#EDE9E2). Shade-card interior notes also cite WW 0020 alongside WW 0005 for industrial-area ceilings with NN 9088 walls.

pairing_notes.contrast: NN9088 (#E9E3D9) to WW0020 (#EDE9E2) is a soft step — ceiling reads slightly cleaner/lighter than wall ecru.
pairing_notes.vs_scheme_a: Scheme A uses warmer linen white WW0005 (#EEEDE9) over mid greige NN9074; Scheme B uses Virgin White WW0020 over light ecru NN9088.
pairing_notes.site_verify: Approve physical NN9088 + WW0020 chips beside granite under morning / afternoon / 3000 K light before ordering.
pairing_notes.shade_card_industrial_note: Shade card interior system notes list ceilings WW 0005 / WW 0020 with walls NN 9088 for industrial areas — aligns with this Scheme B lock.

research_brief.skills_sh_github: No useful interior-design palette-toggle patterns found for this lock; Scheme A/B kept as explicit dual scheme records rather than UI toggle.
